```{ojs}
//| echo: false
buildQuiz = function(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="margin:18px 0 24px 0;text-align:center;">
    <button style="
      display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;
      background:linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea 0%,#764ba2 100%);
      color:#fff;border:none;padding:9px 22px;border-radius:50px;min-height:44px;
      font-size:.95em;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;
      box-shadow:0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45);">
      <span style="font-size:1.1em;">📝</span> ${title}
      <span class="chevron" style="transition:transform .3s;">▼</span>
    </button>
    <div class="quiz-body" style="
      max-height:0;opacity:0;overflow:hidden;
      transition:max-height .5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1),opacity .4s ease,margin-top .3s ease;
      margin-top:0;text-align:left;">
      <button class="close-btn" style="
        display:block;margin:0 auto 10px auto;
        background:rgba(102,126,234,.12);color:#667eea;border:none;
        padding:5px 18px;border-radius:50px;font-size:.85em;min-height:36px;
        font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;">Hide Quiz</button>
      <p style="text-align:center;color:#718096;font-style:italic;font-size:.9em;margin-bottom:12px;">
        Select an answer for each question.</p>
    </div>
  </div>`;
  const toggle = outer.querySelector("button");
  const chevron = toggle.querySelector(".chevron");
  const body   = outer.querySelector(".quiz-body");
  const closeBtn = body.querySelector(".close-btn");
  function expand(){  body.style.maxHeight="3000px";body.style.opacity="1";body.style.marginTop="14px";chevron.style.transform="rotate(180deg)"; }
  function collapse(){ body.style.maxHeight="0";body.style.opacity="0";body.style.marginTop="0";chevron.style.transform="rotate(0)"; }
  toggle.onclick = () => body.style.maxHeight === "0px" || body.style.maxHeight === "" ? expand() : collapse();
  closeBtn.onclick = collapse;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => { b.style.cursor="default"; });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.borderColor="#48bb78";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  return outer;
}
```

# Evidence Review: Revisiting the Performance Task

::: {.engage-box}
## 🕵️ Disproving the climate skeptics

Our goal all unit: **disprove any skeptic who claims humans are not the cause of climate change today, and show why it matters.** At the end of each lesson, your PTO asked you to make and support a claim with that lesson's data. Each skeptic argument below was tested in one lesson:

| Skeptic says... | Tested in |
|---|---|
| "It's just a natural cycle: Earth's orbit or the Sun." | [Earth-Sun Dynamics](unit4-earth-sun-dynamics.qmd) |
| "CO₂ is natural, and CO₂ and temperature are only correlated." | [Climate Feedbacks](unit4-climate-feedbacks.qmd) |
| "Even if it's real, it won't affect people much." | [The Past and the Future](unit4-past-and-future.qmd) |
:::

## Revisiting the Performance Task: Earth-Sun Dynamics {#earth-sun-dynamics}

::: {.evidence-box}
### ☀️ Lesson 4.1: Earth-Sun Dynamics

**PTO prompt (p. 9): Disproving climate skeptics**

<div class="pto-prompt">Using the data about historical temperature changes over time, the changes in orbital factors over the past 9,000 years, the solar cycles, and the effect of solar factors on energy entering Earth's systems, make and support a valid claim about the role of orbital factors and solar cycles on the melting of ice caps today.</div>

**What we figured out:**

- **Orbital factors** (shape of the orbit, degree of tilt, direction of tilt) change how much sunlight reaches **65° N in summer**. They cycle over **tens to hundreds of thousands of years** and match the **glacial-interglacial cycles** (more summer sunlight at 65° N → ice sheets melt → interglacial).
- **From 9,000 years ago to today**, all three factors changed in the direction that gives **weaker northern summers**: tilt dropped from **24.25° to 23.4°**, the Northern Hemisphere now tilts **away** from the Sun when Earth is closest, and the orbit became slightly **less stretched** (146.61–152.59 → 147.06–152.14 million km). Earth **should be slowly cooling toward a glacial period**, not warming.
- **Solar cycles** last about **11 years** and change the Sun's output by only about **1 W/m²** out of ~1,361. Since about **1960, solar output has been flat or slightly falling while temperature has risen about 1 °C.**
- Today's warming of about **1.25 °C took ~140 years**. Natural warming of the same amount took **thousands of years**.

📖 Review the lesson: [Earth-Sun Dynamics](unit4-earth-sun-dynamics.qmd)
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 🔑 Check your thinking (try it first!): a sample claim

**Claim:** Orbital factors and solar cycles are **not** causing the ice caps to melt today.

**Evidence:** Since 9,000 years ago the tilt decreased (24.25° → 23.4°) and the precession flipped, so 65° N summers should be getting weaker and Earth should be moving toward a glacial period. Solar output has been flat or falling since about 1960 while temperature rose about 1 °C. Today's ~1.25 °C rise took ~140 years, compared with thousands of years for natural warming.

**Reasoning:** Ice sheets melt when more energy reaches high northern latitudes in summer. Orbital factors and the Sun are both **reducing** that energy, or not changing it, so something else must be adding energy to Earth's systems.
:::

## Revisiting the Performance Task: Climate Feedbacks {#climate-feedbacks}

::: {.evidence-box}
### 🔄 Lesson 4.2: Climate Feedbacks

**PTO prompt (p. 10): Disproving climate skeptics**

<div class="pto-prompt">Using the data about carbon dioxide levels and temperature changes, the roles of carbon dioxide and ice caps in climate change, and the feedback mechanisms between parts of Earth's systems, make and support a valid claim about the role of carbon dioxide and human activities on the warming of the planet today.</div>

**What we figured out:**

- For **800,000 years**, ice cores show CO₂ stayed between about **180 and 300 ppm**, rising and falling with temperature. Today it is about **421 ppm**.
- **Rate:** CO₂ took about **20,000 years** to rise from 190 to 280 ppm (≈ 0.005 ppm per year), but only about **200 years** to go from 280 to 421 ppm (≈ 0.7 ppm per year), **more than 100 times faster**.
- **Source:** of today's 421.6 ppm, about **134.91 ppm is from human activity** and 286.68 ppm from natural factors. Without humans, CO₂ would be inside the natural range.
- **Carbon cycle model:** before the Industrial Revolution the flows balanced. Now **fossil fuels add 10 Gt of carbon per year** to the atmosphere, and the atmosphere, ocean, and land all gain carbon. Matter is conserved: carbon moved from the **geosphere** to the other reservoirs.
- **Greenhouse effect:** greenhouse gases absorb infrared (heat) from Earth and send some back. Without them Earth would be about **−18 °C**. More CO₂ → more energy kept → higher temperature.
- **Feedbacks:** warming melts **sea ice** → dark ocean absorbs more sunlight (**albedo feedback**) → more warming. That's why the **Arctic is warming almost 4 times faster** than the planet. Warming also makes oceans release CO₂ and **permafrost** release methane and CO₂ (**greenhouse gas feedback**).
- **Disprove the skeptics:** in the ice-core past, temperature sometimes changed **first** (orbital trigger) and CO₂ followed as a feedback. **Today, CO₂ rose first** (from ~285 ppm in 1850) and temperature followed.

📖 Review the lesson: [Climate Feedbacks](unit4-climate-feedbacks.qmd)
:::

Switch between the two quantitative carbon cycle models from your packet.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
u4cCarbon = ({
  "Pre-Industrial Revolution": {
    stores: {"Atmosphere": 560, "Ocean": 38000, "Land biomass": 2160, "Fossil fuels": 10000},
    flows: [["Ocean","Atmosphere",62],["Atmosphere","Ocean",60],["Land biomass","Atmosphere",107],["Atmosphere","Land biomass",109],["Fossil fuels","Atmosphere",0]]
  },
  "Post-Industrial Revolution": {
    stores: {"Atmosphere": 840, "Ocean": 41000, "Land biomass": 2500, "Fossil fuels": 9000},
    flows: [["Ocean","Atmosphere",77.5],["Atmosphere","Ocean",80],["Land biomass","Atmosphere",120],["Atmosphere","Land biomass",122.5],["Fossil fuels","Atmosphere",10]]
  }
})
viewof u4cCarbonPick = Inputs.radio(Object.keys(u4cCarbon), {label: "Carbon cycle model:", value: "Post-Industrial Revolution"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const m = u4cCarbon[u4cCarbonPick];
  const res = Object.keys(m.stores);
  const net = res.map(r => {
    const inn = d3.sum(m.flows.filter(f => f[1] === r), f => f[2]);
    const out = d3.sum(m.flows.filter(f => f[0] === r), f => f[2]);
    return {reservoir: r, inn, out, net: +(inn - out).toFixed(1), store: m.stores[r]};
  });
  const wrap = d3.create("div");
  wrap.append(() => Plot.plot({
    title: `Net change in carbon each year: ${u4cCarbonPick}`,
    subtitle: "Gigatons of carbon per year (in − out), from Tables 1 and 2 in your packet",
    width: width, height: 220, marginLeft: 96, marginRight: 50,
    x: {label: "Net change (Gt C per year) →", domain: [-11, 11], grid: true},
    y: {label: null, domain: res},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(net, {y: "reservoir", x: "net", fill: d => d.net > 0 ? "#c62828" : d.net < 0 ? "#0277bd" : "#90a4ae", tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.reservoir}\nIn: ${d.inn} Gt/yr  Out: ${d.out} Gt/yr\nNet: ${d.net > 0 ? "+" : ""}${d.net} Gt/yr\nStored: ${d.store.toLocaleString()} Gt`}),
      Plot.text(net.filter(d => d.net >= 0), {y: "reservoir", x: "net", text: d => `${d.net > 0 ? "+" : ""}${d.net}`, dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fill: "currentColor", fontWeight: "bold"}),
      Plot.text(net.filter(d => d.net < 0), {y: "reservoir", x: "net", text: d => `${d.net}`, dx: -6, textAnchor: "end", fill: "currentColor", fontWeight: "bold"}),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }));
  const rows = net.map(d => `<tr><td style="padding:4px 8px;">${d.reservoir}</td><td style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:right;">${d.store.toLocaleString()}</td><td style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:right;">${d.inn}</td><td style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:right;">${d.out}</td><td style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:right;font-weight:700;">${d.net > 0 ? "+" : ""}${d.net}</td></tr>`).join("");
  wrap.append("div").style("overflow-x", "auto").html(`<table style="width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:.9em;background:#fff;color:#1a1a1a;border-radius:8px;">
    <thead><tr style="background:#e0f7fa;"><th style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:left;">Reservoir</th><th style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:right;">Stored (Gt)</th><th style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:right;">In</th><th style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:right;">Out</th><th style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:right;">Net</th></tr></thead><tbody>${rows}</tbody></table>`);
  wrap.append("div").style("background", "#fff").style("color", "#1a1a1a").style("border-left", "6px solid #00838f").style("border-radius", "10px").style("padding", "12px 16px").style("margin", "10px 0")
    .html(u4cCarbonPick.startsWith("Pre")
      ? "<b>Balanced:</b> every reservoir's in = out (net 0). The carbon cycle was stable, so CO₂ stayed in its natural range."
      : "<b>Out of balance:</b> fossil fuels lose 10 Gt/yr. The atmosphere gains <b>+5 Gt/yr</b>, and the ocean and land each gain +2.5 Gt/yr. The extra carbon came from burning fossil fuels.");
  return wrap.node();
}
```

## 🔑 Check your thinking (try it first!): a sample claim

**Claim:** Human activities, mainly burning fossil fuels, have raised CO₂ to levels not seen in 800,000 years, and that extra CO₂ is warming the planet today.

**Evidence:** CO₂ is ~421 ppm vs. a natural range of ~180–300 ppm; ~135 ppm of it is from humans; it rose more than 100× faster than at the end of the ice age; the carbon cycle model shows fossil fuels adding 10 Gt C/yr; since 1850 CO₂ rose first and temperature followed; the Arctic is warming almost 4× faster than the globe as sea ice melts.

**Reasoning:** CO₂ absorbs infrared energy leaving Earth and sends some back, so more CO₂ means more energy stays in Earth's systems. Melting ice lowers albedo, so more sunlight is absorbed, a positive feedback that speeds up warming. Warmer oceans and thawing permafrost release more greenhouse gases, another positive feedback.
:::

- Include current greenhouse gas levels and their sources, how the greenhouse effect works, the melting of northern ice caps, and **albedo and greenhouse gas feedback loops**. Explain why this is **cause, not just correlation**.
:::

## Revisiting the Performance Task: The Past and the Future {#the-past-and-the-future}

::: {.evidence-box}
### 🌊 Lesson 4.3: The Past and the Future

**PTO prompt (p. 11, titled "Greenhouse Gases 5E"): Disproving climate skeptics**

<div class="pto-prompt">Using the data about projected temperature changes, other projected climate changes, and information about their role in shaping human lives, make and support a claim about how human populations will likely be impacted by climate related hazards in the near future.</div>

**What we figured out:**

- **Past climate change shaped people.** Early humans who left Africa ~120,000 years ago died out in a drought. The **Clovis culture** in North America disappeared about **12,750 years ago**, at the same time as a sudden cold snap (the **Younger Dryas**).
- **Melting ice raises sea level.** As the ice sheets melted after 20,000 years ago, sea level rose about **120 meters**, flooding land bridges and coastlines.
- **Melting ice can slow ocean currents.** Fresh meltwater is less dense, so it doesn't sink. That slows the **AMOC**, which carries heat north. Less heat moves north and northern air temperatures drop. Continued melting today could slow the AMOC again.
- **Forecasting:** satellite data show sea level rising about **3 mm per year** (32 years of data): about **15 cm (6 in) in 50 years** and **30 cm (12 in) in 100 years** if the rate stayed the same. It is actually speeding up.
- **Scenarios:** climate models project about **1.8, 2.7, 3.6, or 4.4 °C** of warming by 2080, depending on how much fossil fuel we burn (SSP1-2.6 to SSP5-8.5). More warming → more sea level rise, heat, and changing rain.
- **Impacts on people are already happening:** glacial lake floods (about **15 million** people at risk), landslides, coastlines in Alaska shrinking **more than 3 ft per year**, collapsing fisheries (snow crab), crop losses and hunger, and **27 billion-dollar weather disasters in the U.S. in 2024** (average 9).

📖 Review the lesson: [The Past and the Future](unit4-past-and-future.qmd)
:::

## 🔑 Check your thinking (try it first!): a sample claim

**Claim:** In the near future, climate-related hazards will displace more people, damage coastal communities, and threaten food and water supplies, and the impacts grow with every degree of warming.

**Evidence:** Sea level is rising ~3 mm/yr (≈ 15 cm in 50 years at minimum); models project 1.8–4.4 °C of warming by 2080; 15 million people are at risk from glacial lake floods; Alaskan coastlines are eroding more than 3 ft/yr; U.S. billion-dollar disasters reached 27 in 2024 compared with an average of 9; 20.3 million people were forced to move by weather disasters in 2023. In the past, rapid climate change caused populations like the Clovis to collapse.

**Reasoning:** Warming melts ice, which raises sea level and can slow the AMOC. Warmer air holds more water, which fuels stronger storms and floods. These hazards push people from their homes and disrupt crops and fisheries.
:::

## 🔁 Back to the Tell the Story texts

At the start of the unit you read three "texts" ([Unit Opening](unit4-opening.qmd)):

1. **Arctic temperature over the last 2,000 years:** slow cooling for almost 2,000 years, then a sharp rise after about 1880 (direct measurements).
2. **Climate-related displacement in 2023:** at least **6.6 million people** displaced, **20.3 million** forced moves; floods (**9.8 million**) and storms (**9.5 million**) caused most.
3. **Scientists vs. the public:** **99.9%** of research papers agree humans cause climate change, but only **57%** of people think scientists agree, and **63%** say they are worried.

**Now you can explain them.** Review your ideas for **why scientists are sure humans are causing climate change, and why it's a problem.**
:::

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Why scientists are so sure: many lines of evidence point the same way

1. **Natural causes are ruled out:** orbit and Sun point toward cooling or no change.
2. **The cause is measured:** CO₂ is far above its 800,000-year range, and the extra carbon comes from fossil fuels.
3. **The mechanism is known:** the greenhouse effect, boosted by albedo and greenhouse gas feedbacks.
4. **The rate is unusual:** both CO₂ and temperature are changing faster than in any natural event in the record.

**Why it matters:** rising seas, stronger floods and storms, heat, and food disruptions are already displacing people, and the amount of future harm depends on human choices.
:::

## 📣 Share with the community

**For this final task, communicate to someone in your community who is skeptical about climate change.** In a **letter, public service announcement, pamphlet, or other format**:

1. **Explain how the data demonstrates human causes** of climate change
2. **Describe the ongoing and future impacts** on the planet of climate change
3. **Explain how these changes are likely to affect people in your community**

If you choose something with video or audio, write the script in your PTO.
:::

## What Your Communication Must Include

| Be sure to include... | Evidence from |
|---|---|
| 1. How the **data shows human causes** | [Earth-Sun Dynamics](#earth-sun-dynamics) (natural causes ruled out), [Climate Feedbacks](#climate-feedbacks) (CO₂ levels, sources, greenhouse effect) |
| 2. **Ongoing and future impacts** on the planet | [Climate Feedbacks](#climate-feedbacks) (melting ice, feedbacks), [The Past and the Future](#the-past-and-the-future) (sea level, AMOC, warming scenarios) |
| 3. How the changes will likely **affect people in your community** | [The Past and the Future](#the-past-and-the-future) (displacement, food, disasters), [Your Community](#your-community-new-york-city) |

## Your Community: New York City {#your-community-new-york-city}

Most students using this book live in **New York City**, a coastal city of about 8 million people with **520 miles of waterfront**. If you live somewhere else, look up the same kinds of facts for your community.

| NYC hazard | What has already happened | Link to the unit |
|---|---|---|
| 🌊 **Sea level rise** | The sea at the Battery (Lower Manhattan) has risen about **1.5 feet since 1850**, roughly twice the global average because the land is also slowly sinking. | Melting ice, ~3 mm/yr global rise |
| 🌀 **Storm surge** | **Hurricane Sandy (2012)** pushed a record storm tide of about **14 feet** at the Battery, killed **44 people** in NYC, and caused about **$19 billion** in damage in the city. Higher seas make every future surge reach farther. | Sea level rise + storms |
| 🌧️ **Extreme rain** | **Hurricane Ida's remnants (2021)** dropped a record **3.15 inches of rain in one hour** in Central Park. **13 New Yorkers died**, most in flooded basement apartments. | Warmer air holds more water |
| 🔥 **Extreme heat** | Heat is NYC's deadliest weather: about **350 deaths a year** are linked to hot weather, hitting older people and neighborhoods with fewer trees and less air conditioning hardest. | Projected warming scenarios |

<p style="font-size:.85em;">Sources: NYC Panel on Climate Change; NOAA National Hurricane Center; National Weather Service; NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (Heat-Related Mortality Report, 2022). Numbers are rounded.</p>

::: {.claim-box}
### 📌 CLAIM
Tell your skeptic, in one or two sentences, **what is happening and why**. Example starter:

- "The climate is warming because humans are adding CO₂ by burning fossil fuels, and that is already putting [your neighborhood] at risk from ___."
:::

::: {.evidence-box}
### 📊 EVIDENCE
Pick **specific numbers** a skeptic can check: tilt 24.25° → 23.4°, solar output flat since 1960, CO₂ ~421 ppm vs. 180–300 ppm, ~135 ppm from humans, +10 Gt C/yr from fossil fuels, Arctic warming ~4×, sea level ~3 mm/yr, 1.8–4.4 °C by 2080, 27 billion-dollar disasters in 2024, Sandy's ~14 ft storm tide.
:::

::: {.reasoning-box}
### 🧠 REASONING
Connect each number to the science: *Orbital factors should be cooling us, so they can't cause today's warming. Burning fossil fuels moves carbon from the geosphere into the atmosphere, where CO₂ traps infrared energy. The extra energy melts ice, which lowers albedo and raises sea level, so storm surges like Sandy's will reach more neighborhoods.*
:::

```{ojs}
    {id: "p1", label: "1️⃣ How the data shows HUMAN causes (2–3 pieces of evidence + reasoning)", rows: 4},
    {id: "p2", label: "2️⃣ Ongoing and future impacts on the planet (ice, feedbacks, sea level, AMOC, warming scenarios)", rows: 4},
    {id: "p3", label: "3️⃣ How this will likely affect people in YOUR community (name places and hazards)", rows: 4},
    {id: "close", label: "✅ Closing: why it matters / what you want them to think or do", rows: 2}
  ];
  const formats = ["Letter", "Public service announcement (script)", "Pamphlet", "Social media post / infographic", "Video or podcast script", "Other"];
  const box = html`<div class="u4c-planner u4c-card" style="background:#fff;color:#1a1a1a;border-radius:14px;padding:16px;box-shadow:0 2px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.12);border-top:6px solid #00838f;"></div>`;
  const fmtWrap = html`<label style="display:block;font-weight:700;margin-bottom:10px;">📄 Format
    <select style="display:block;min-height:44px;margin-top:4px;border:2px solid #b2ebf2;border-radius:8px;padding:6px;background:#fff;color:#1a1a1a;">${formats.map(f => html`<option>${f}</option>`)}</select></label>`;
  const fmt = fmtWrap.querySelector("select");
  if (saved.format) fmt.value = saved.format;
  box.appendChild(fmtWrap);
  const areas = {};
  fields.forEach(f => {
    const lab = html`<label style="display:block;font-weight:700;margin:10px 0 4px;">${f.label}
      <textarea rows="${f.rows}" style="display:block;margin-top:4px;border:2px solid #b2ebf2;border-radius:8px;padding:8px;font:inherit;font-weight:400;background:#fff;color:#1a1a1a;"></textarea></label>`;
    const ta = lab.querySelector("textarea");
    ta.value = saved[f.id] || "";
    areas[f.id] = ta;
    box.appendChild(lab);
  });
  const status = html`<div style="font-size:.85em;color:#00695c;min-height:1.2em;margin-top:6px;"></div>`;
  const preview = html`<div style="white-space:pre-wrap;background:#f1f8f9;border-radius:8px;padding:12px;margin-top:10px;font-size:.92em;display:none;"></div>`;
  const btnStyle = "min-height:44px;padding:8px 16px;border:none;border-radius:50px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;margin:8px 8px 0 0;";
  const bPrev = html`<button style="${btnStyle}background:#00838f;color:#fff;">👀 Preview outline</button>`;
  const bCopy = html`<button style="${btnStyle}background:#0277bd;color:#fff;">📋 Copy outline</button>`;
  const bClear = html`<button style="${btnStyle}background:#eceff1;color:#37474f;">🗑️ Clear</button>`;
  const outline = () => [
    `FORMAT: ${fmt.value}`, `AUDIENCE: ${areas.who.value}`, `SKEPTIC CLAIM I'M ANSWERING: ${areas.claim.value}`, "",
    `1. HOW THE DATA SHOWS HUMAN CAUSES:\n${areas.p1.value}`, "",
    `2. ONGOING AND FUTURE IMPACTS:\n${areas.p2.value}`, "",
    `3. EFFECTS ON MY COMMUNITY:\n${areas.p3.value}`, "",
    `CLOSING:\n${areas.close.value}`
  ].join("\n");
  const save = () => {
    const data = {format: fmt.value};
    fields.forEach(f => data[f.id] = areas[f.id].value);
    try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(data)); status.textContent = "Saved in this browser."; } catch (e) { status.textContent = "Couldn't save in this browser. Copy your outline before leaving."; }
  };
  box.addEventListener("input", save);
  fmt.addEventListener("change", save);
  bPrev.onclick = () => { preview.textContent = outline(); preview.style.display = "block"; };
  bCopy.onclick = async () => {
    const text = outline();
    try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text); status.textContent = "Copied! Paste it into your document or PTO."; }
    catch (e) { preview.textContent = text; preview.style.display = "block"; status.textContent = "Copy isn't available here. Select the outline below and copy it."; }
  };
  bClear.onclick = () => {
    fields.forEach(f => areas[f.id].value = ""); preview.style.display = "none";
    try { localStorage.removeItem(KEY); } catch (e) {}
    status.textContent = "Cleared.";
  };
  const row = html`<div></div>`;
  row.append(bPrev, bCopy, bClear);
  box.append(row, status, preview);
  return box;
}
```

- Use evidence from **all three lessons** and cover **all three points**: human causes, ongoing and future impacts, and effects on your community.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
u4cChecklist = {
  const groups = [
    {title: "1️⃣ The data shows human causes", items: [
      "Shows orbital factors (9 kya → today) should be weakening northern summers, so they can't explain melting ice caps",
      "Shows solar output has been flat or falling since ~1960 while temperature rose (solar cycles are ~11 years and small)",
      "Compares rates: ~1.25 °C in ~140 years today vs. thousands of years in natural warming",
      "Gives today's CO₂ (~421 ppm) vs. the 800,000-year range (~180–300 ppm) and its source (fossil fuels, ~135 ppm from humans)",
      "Explains the greenhouse effect mechanism (CO₂ absorbs infrared and sends energy back to Earth)",
      "Explains why it is cause, not just correlation (mechanism + CO₂ rose first since 1850)"
    ]},
    {title: "2️⃣ Ongoing and future impacts on the planet", items: [
      "Describes melting northern ice caps and the Arctic warming ~4× faster",
      "Explains positive feedback loops: albedo (sea ice) and greenhouse gases (ocean CO₂, permafrost methane)",
      "Uses forecasts: sea level ~3 mm/yr and rising, warming scenarios of 1.8–4.4 °C by 2080",
      "Describes the possible AMOC slowdown and what it would do to heat transport"
    ]},
    {title: "3️⃣ Effects on people in your community", items: [
      "Names your community and its specific hazards (e.g., NYC: sea level rise, storm surge, extreme rain, heat)",
      "Uses evidence that people are already affected (displacement, disasters, food supplies, melting ice)",
      "Explains how changes could increase displacement and migration, including lessons from the past (Clovis, early humans)"
    ]},
    {title: "🗣️ Communication", items: [
      "Written for a skeptic: answers at least one skeptic claim respectfully",
      "Every claim is linked to evidence with scientific reasoning (CER)",
      "Uses evidence from all three lessons",
      "Chosen format fits the audience (letter, PSA, pamphlet, script...)"
    ]}
  ];
  const total = d3.sum(groups, g => g.items.length);
  const box = html`<div class="u4c-card" style="background:#fff;color:#1a1a1a;border-radius:14px;padding:16px;box-shadow:0 2px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.12);"></div>`;
  const bar = html`<div style="background:#eceff1;border-radius:20px;height:14px;overflow:hidden;margin:4px 0 4px;"><div style="background:linear-gradient(90deg,#00838f,#c62828);height:100%;width:0%;transition:width .3s;"></div></div>`;
  const label = html`<div style="font-weight:700;font-size:.95em;"></div>`;
  box.append(label, bar);
  const update = () => {
    const n = box.querySelectorAll("input:checked").length;
    bar.firstChild.style.width = `${100 * n / total}%`;
    label.textContent = n === total ? `🎉 ${n} of ${total}: ready to share!` : `${n} of ${total} included`;
  };
  groups.forEach(g => {
    box.appendChild(html`<div style="font-weight:800;margin:14px 0 4px;color:#00695c;">${g.title}</div>`);
    g.items.forEach(it => {
      const lab = html`<label style="display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:flex-start;padding:8px 6px;min-height:44px;border-bottom:1px solid #eceff1;cursor:pointer;">
        <input type="checkbox" style="width:22px;height:22px;flex:0 0 22px;margin-top:2px;accent-color:#00838f;"><span>${it}</span></label>`;
      lab.querySelector("input").onchange = update;
      box.appendChild(lab);
    });
  });
  update();
  return box;
}
```

# Unit Summary

| Big idea | What the evidence shows |
|---|---|
| **The phenomenon** | Earth, especially the Arctic, is warming fast. 99.9% of climate research agrees humans are the cause, but many people are unsure. Climate hazards displaced people 20.3 million times in 2023 |
| **Earth-Sun Dynamics** | Orbital factors (eccentricity, tilt, precession) drive ice ages over 10,000s–100,000s of years and today point toward cooling. The ~11-year solar cycle is too small and short; solar output has been flat since ~1960 |
| **Climate Feedbacks** | CO₂ (~421 ppm) is far above its 800,000-year range because burning fossil fuels moved carbon into the atmosphere. The greenhouse effect traps more energy; albedo and greenhouse gas feedbacks amplify warming, so the Arctic warms ~4× faster |
| **The Past and the Future** | Past rapid climate change (Younger Dryas, AMOC slowdown) affected human populations. Sea level is rising ~3 mm/yr; models project 1.8–4.4 °C by 2080 depending on emissions; floods, storms, heat, and food disruption are increasing |
| **Why it matters** | Climate hazards are already affecting communities like NYC (Sandy, Ida, heat). How much worse it gets depends on human choices, which you'll explore in Unit 6 |

# End-of-Unit Quiz

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function buildUnit4Quiz(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; max-width:720px; margin:18px auto;"></div>`;
  const header = html`<div style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#01579b 0%,#00838f 100%);color:#fff;border-radius:14px 14px 0 0;padding:18px 24px;">
    <div style="font-size:1.1em;font-weight:700;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;color:#fff;"><span style="font-size:1.2em;">📝</span> ${title}</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.9;margin-top:4px;color:#fff;">Select an answer for each question.</div>
  </div>`;
  const body = html`<div style="border:1.5px solid #b2ebf2;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 14px 14px;overflow:hidden;background:#f5fbfc;padding:16px;"></div>`;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => {
          b.style.cursor="default"; b.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0"; b.style.background="#f8fafc"; b.style.color="#475569";
        });
        const correctBtn = card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct];
        correctBtn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";correctBtn.style.background="#f0fff4";correctBtn.style.color="#276749";correctBtn.style.fontWeight="700";
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";btn.style.color="#9b2c2c";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  outer.appendChild(header);
  outer.appendChild(body);
  return outer;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
buildUnit4Quiz("u4c-summative-quiz", "🌡️ End-of-Unit Quiz — Why Are Scientists So Sure?", [
  {
    q: "Glacial-interglacial cycles repeat about every 100,000 years. Which factor best matches that timescale?",
    options: ["The ~11-year solar cycle", "Changes in Earth's orbit and tilt (orbital factors)", "Daily weather", "Yearly seasons"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "Orbital factors change over tens to hundreds of thousands of years and change how much summer sunlight reaches 65° N, which controls whether ice sheets grow or melt."
  },
  {
    q: "On the 22,000-year temperature graph, warming of about 1.25 °C at the end of the ice age took about 5,000 years. Today's took about 140 years. What does this rate difference suggest?",
    options: ["Today's warming has the same cause as the ice age ending", "Today's warming is far too fast to be explained by slow orbital changes, so a different cause is needed", "Temperature data are unreliable", "Warming always takes 140 years"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "Orbital changes act over thousands of years, and right now they point toward cooling. A change this fast needs a fast cause: the rapid rise in greenhouse gases."
  },
  {
    q: "A student graphs solar output and global temperature from 1880 to 2014. Which pattern would show the Sun is NOT causing recent warming?",
    options: ["Both rise together the whole time", "Solar output stays flat or falls after ~1960 while temperature keeps rising", "Temperature falls with solar output", "Both stay flat"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "That is exactly what the NASA graph shows. If the Sun were the cause, temperature would follow solar output."
  },
  {
    q: "Ice cores show CO₂ between about 180 and 300 ppm for 800,000 years. Today it's about 421 ppm. Which explanation is best supported?",
    options: ["A natural cycle that happens every 100,000 years", "Burning fossil fuels moved carbon from the geosphere into the atmosphere faster than oceans and land can absorb it", "Volcanoes erupted more in the last 200 years", "Plants stopped photosynthesizing"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "The carbon cycle model shows fossil fuels adding 10 Gt C/yr and the atmosphere gaining +5 Gt/yr. CO₂ rose more than 100× faster than at the end of the ice age."
  },
  {
    q: "In the pre-industrial carbon cycle model, the atmosphere received 62 + 107 = 169 Gt/yr and released 60 + 109 = 169 Gt/yr. What does this mean?",
    options: ["The atmosphere was gaining carbon", "The cycle was balanced: carbon moved, but the amount in the atmosphere stayed steady", "Carbon was being destroyed", "The ocean was losing all its carbon"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "In = out means a net change of 0. Carbon (matter) is conserved as it moves between reservoirs; only fossil fuel burning upset that balance."
  },
  {
    q: "Which sequence correctly describes the albedo feedback loop?",
    options: ["Warming → sea ice melts → darker ocean absorbs more sunlight → more warming", "Warming → more ice → more reflection → more warming", "Cooling → ice melts → cooling", "Sunlight → ice grows → warming"],
    correct: 0,
    explanation: "Ice reflects most sunlight; dark ocean absorbs it. Losing ice adds more energy, which melts more ice. This positive feedback is why the Arctic warms almost 4× faster than the globe."
  },
  {
    q: "About 12,900 years ago, a sudden cold snap (the Younger Dryas) hit the Northern Hemisphere as ice sheets melted. What is the best explanation?",
    options: ["The Sun turned off", "Fresh meltwater lowered the density of North Atlantic water, slowing the AMOC so less heat reached the north", "CO₂ suddenly doubled", "Earth's tilt flipped"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "Less salty water is less dense and doesn't sink, which weakens the AMOC. The Clovis culture disappeared around the same time, showing climate shifts can affect populations."
  },
  {
    q: "Satellite data show sea level rising about 3 mm per year. What's the best prediction for the next 50 years if the rate stays the same, and why is it a low estimate?",
    options: ["About 15 cm (6 in); the rate is speeding up as ice melts faster", "About 3 mm; sea level never changes", "About 50 m; all the ice will melt", "It will fall because of the AMOC"],
    correct: 0,
    explanation: "3 mm × 50 = 150 mm ≈ 15 cm. Faster melting and warmer, expanding oceans are increasing the rate, so the real rise is likely more."
  },
  {
    q: "Models project 1.8 °C of warming by 2080 under SSP1-2.6 and 4.4 °C under SSP5-8.5. What is the main difference between these scenarios?",
    options: ["How much fossil fuel humans burn", "Which climate model was used", "Changes in Earth's orbit", "The number of sunspots"],
    correct: 0,
    explanation: "The scenarios are based on future greenhouse gas emissions. This means human choices strongly affect how big future climate impacts will be."
  },
  {
    q: "You are writing to a skeptical NYC neighbor. Which sentence best connects the evidence to your community?",
    options: ["\"Climate change is bad, trust me.\"", "\"Burning fossil fuels has raised CO₂ to ~421 ppm, warming the planet and melting ice; seas at the Battery have already risen ~1.5 ft, so storm surges like Sandy's will reach more of our neighborhoods.\"", "\"The Sun is getting hotter, so NYC will flood.\"", "\"Climate change only affects polar bears.\""],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "A strong communication links a human cause (CO₂ from fossil fuels), the science (warming, melting ice, sea level rise), and a specific local impact with data."
  }
])
```
